Heey everyone,

It's probably not the best place to show a tool for offline parties with a guitar, but I still wanna try :D

My brain and fingers produced something great in the last few months and it's called Kantamigo. If you're a guitarist or participated a party where everybody sing together, then you probably had a "what's the lyrics?" situation when you want to sing but you have no idea what the guitarist is playing. So this is what Kantamigo for - realtime lyrics for guitar parties. It's also a personal songbook of course, with many cool features (smart import from ANY source, not-so-stupid auto-scroll, pedal / keyboard support, playlists, tuner, transponder and so on).

So if it's relevant for you - please give it a try, and please please let me know what do you think. I've been having that idea in my head for ~4 years, finally created it and really want to hear if I'm not the only one who needs this :)

Thanks!

story_text.value:
I was working (with agents) on testing out various attention algorithm ideas I had, and I found that the existing infrastructure/libraries made it more difficult than it should be.

So I created Jacq, a DSL and compiler. A jacq file describes a model’s configuration, weights, layers, and pipeline. Jacq turns it into a standalone CUDA inference runtime and a Python weight exporter. Kernel descriptions can also generate CUDA harnesses.

The easiest way to try it is the TinyLlama example in the README. Building, validating, visualizing, and generating CUDA only require Rust. Of course, running inference does require an NVIDIA GPU, CUDA, Python dependencies, and weights. Jacq doesn't support other GPU vendors (AMD, etc) or Metal, yet (PR's welcome!)

There's also an experimental vLLM patch to compile and patch your jacq file into a vLLM build, as well.

Feedback very welcome!

title.value: Show HN: Jacq, a DSL that compiles model and kernel descriptions to CUDA

story_text.value:
This scratches an itch I experience most months. When you get a "super handy QR Code" from a service, like Asos, Vinted and others that means you have to physically go to a post office to post your parcel. About ten years ago this was revolutionary convenience, but now it's a frustration.

If you're like me you use Royal Mail's collection service to ship most of your parcels/returns from home, and post offices are open for ridiculously narrow times of day these days. Royal Mail don't provide an online facility to create a label from these in-person QR codes, so I built one instead.

Behold, Citizen - Prince of Post! https://princeofpost.com

I had some fun designing this, and it's something that I'll genuinely use all the time, so I thought I'd share it for others with this problem too. I couldn't find any prior art, but if you want to ruin my day please do tell me about anywhere that does this already :-)

story_text.value:
I built Coldframe, a honeypot that pretends to be a supermarket refrigeration controller. Inspired by the events on industrial fridge installations in the past weeks, I wanted to see what people would try against a convincing fake.

To learn more about this I built a honeypot that resembled perfectly the Danfoss AK-SM 800A and Dixell XWEB interfaces. Both of them are recognized on Shodan as real ones (an not as honeypots). It’s one Python file using only the standard library, and it builds on eppser/danfoss-ak-sm-decoy and public research by Synacktiv, Claroty and Ironhackers.

Things that were fun to get right:

- Matching real units. I used Shodan records of real devices to match header order, page titles, certificate fields and TLS versions. The Danfoss persona sends nginx headers in the same order as a real AK-SM 800A. The Dixell persona sends no Server header and pads its page to exactly 8,202 bytes.

- Recognising exploit attempts. It recognises CVE-2025-41450, the Danfoss “code of the day” login bypass, and records whether the submitted code is correct for today. It also tags attempts targeting three other Danfoss CVEs and the XWEB vulnerabilities.

- Letting them in. Default logins open a fake store dashboard with defrost buttons, so you see the second move, not just the first. Nothing behind it is real.

Two instances have been live for a day. So far they’ve only seen generic scanners and Shodan’s crawler, which is called refrigerator.census.shodan.io.

Feedback welcome, especially from anyone who has seen these devices in the field!

story_text.value:
Hi HN,

Vondet is a planning board, but you don't write on it. Claude writes to Vondet via an MCP connection.

As I worked on my product with Claude, my Markdown files gradually piled up. There were files like “beta plan”, “v1 plan”, and “development plan v0.5.” I asked Claude to tidy them up. It created a new file “next-milestone plan v0.1” Haha.

I spent too much time trying to remember what I planned. So I built a tool to keep plans and decisions in one place. It's ready for Claude to refer to in future sessions.

Claude can use the board to: - Read: Tasks, decision logs, topics - Plan: Capture, update, and order tasks - Record: Decisions

Vondet works through your conversation with Claude via MCP. I would appreciate it if you could try it in your own Claude.

How to try it: 1. Sign up at Vondet(Magic link, Github, and Google login are supported). 2. Connect MCP to your Claude. 3. Try asking Claude to record a development plan on the board.

How do you all manage your development plans and tasks? I would appreciate any feedback, and interest.

story_text.value:
Solous is a private journaling app. This app is inspired by movies like inside out or Yumi's Cells where we all have emotions inside us. When we write it is one of our emotions writing it. We want to talk to ourselves between these debating ideas and emotions. We are solo but also there are persons inside us. That's where the name is from solo-us. In Solous, you can reply to your own message anytime. It supports normal stuff like tag and search. I try to make it as secure as possible with e2ee as an option.

I am the sole builder of the app. I built this app mostly for myself in my free time with Claude. Yes I vibed 100% but I am familiar with aws and python, I am a decent programmer. It is true that these days, everyone can do that. But it still takes time and effort to make it run smoothly and polish features and make it easy to use. I don't believe the future of software is everyone vibe their own stuff. The most efficient way is still to use several good apps. I think there may be more diversity instead of everyone use app store or play store.

Because it is made for myself, it has no reminder emails, sometimes, I even don't journal for days, but I feel good when I write one. I think it is good to record what happened in life. Especially when I feel bad.

And it is private, it has two factor login, security keys such as face id or whatever you use to unlock your phone, and it has optional end to end encryption. At first I want to make it default, but then I realized it takes some time to setup and maybe it will reduce conversion. so I leave it for whoever care about privacy.

The app is free for now. For free tier, there is 1GB limit on uploads and how many journaling you can do (if you write on your own not using ai, you will be ok with free tier). Later I will charge money if you need more space and maybe if you want to give me more money, you can become member and maybe I will open some private features for members or provide more customization options. That's the idea. I will be around today, please try and let me know. Thank you!
